publications.title: The Effectiveness and Toxicity of Frameless CyberKnife Based Radiosurgery for Parkinson's Disease-Phase II Study.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Prospective open-label single-arm phase II trial (NCT02406105) of frameless CyberKnife radiosurgery for Parkinson disease tremor. The planned sample was 27 patients. The primary endpoint was safety.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Single-fraction radiosurgery. The dose was prescribed as 100% at the central point, and the whole target was covered by the 80% isodose. The total dose ranged from 70 to 105 Gy and was escalated by 5 Gy after every three patients, with at least 3 months of toxicity observation before the next step.

Randomization will be stratified by metastasis volume and histology.

At the same time, tissue and peripheral blood samples of patients were collected for the determination of PD-L1 expression, ctDNA and other biomarkers and results analysis to find prognostic or curative effect predictors. Patients with advanced melanoma who met the inclusion criteria but did not meet the exclusion criteria were enrolled in the study and received PD-1 inhibitors with or without radiotherapy.

registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: For patients with non-small cell lung cancer and more than five metastatic lesions (non-oligometastatic disease), does radical treatment of the primary lung lesion, in addition to pharmacotherapy, also provide benefits in terms of progression-free survival (PFS) and local control? Currently, there is limited clinical research on combining pharmacotherapy with radiotherapy for the primary lesion in non-oligometastatic patients. Therefore, this study aims to investigate whether radical radiotherapy targeting the primary lung lesion, in addition to pharmacotherapy, can improve local control and survival in non-oligometastatic patients, and whether the associated toxicities are acceptable.

eligibility: Histologic high-grade Ta, high-grade T1, or Tis (CIS only) urothelial carcinoma within 120 days before randomization. Variant histology is allowed if predominantly urothelial.
No neuroendocrine component (small cell or large cell). No pure squamous cell carcinoma or pure adenocarcinoma.

All visible papillary lesions macroscopically resected by TURBT within 90 days before randomization (residual CIS allowed). If the treating urologist did not perform the TURBT, that urologist must do a cystoscopy within 45 days before randomization confirming no visible papillary disease.
High-grade T1 requires a restaging TURBT within 90 days before randomization. A restaging TURBT with no residual cancer is still eligible based on the prior TURBT.

BCG-exposed NMIBC: any high-grade recurrence within 24 months of induction-only BCG; high-grade papillary Ta/T1 recurrence 6-24 months after induction plus maintenance BCG; or high-grade CIS (with or without Ta/T1) recurrence 12-24 months after induction plus maintenance BCG. BCG-naive patients and those 25 months or more from last BCG are not eligible. TURBT up to 26 months from the last instillation is allowed if recurrence was evident or suspected within 24 months.

No BCG-unresponsive disease: persistent or recurrent high-grade Ta/T1 less than 6 months after adequate BCG, high-grade CIS recurrence less than 12 months after adequate BCG, or high-grade T1 at the first 3-month assessment after induction. Adequate BCG is at least 5 of 6 induction doses plus at least 2 of 3 maintenance doses or at least 2 of 6 repeat-induction doses within 6 months. A patient who previously met BCG-unresponsive criteria but no longer does may enroll if the urologist considers BCG re-treatment reasonable.

Prior intravesical chemotherapy (including gemcitabine, gemcitabine/docetaxel, or TAR-200) and prior systemic or intravesical agents for NMIBC (including pembrolizumab or other checkpoint inhibitors, nadofaragene firadenovec, nogapendekin alfa inbakicept, cretostimogene) are allowed. More than one prior BCG induction course or prior maintenance is allowed.

No history of intolerance to BCG (stopping induction or maintenance for toxicity) or to any other intravesical therapy. No compromised bladder function that makes further intravesical therapy unlikely to be tolerated.

No prior or current muscle-invasive (T2-T4), locally advanced unresectable, or metastatic urothelial carcinoma on CT or MRI of the abdomen and pelvis within 120 days before randomization (contrast preferred, CT or MR urogram preferred; noncontrast allowed if contrast is contraindicated).

Prior upper tract urothelial carcinoma is allowed if localized Ta, T1, or Tis, definitively treated by nephroureterectomy or ureterectomy, with at least one post-treatment imaging study showing no residual upper tract disease.
Non-invasive (Ta/Tis) prostatic urethral urothelial carcinoma is allowed if TURP is done before enrollment and shows no lamina propria or prostatic stromal invasion.

HIV-infected patients on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months are eligible. A prior or concurrent malignancy is allowed if it does not interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Age 18 or older. Not pregnant and not nursing; pregnancy test within 14 days before randomization for persons of childbearing potential.

Most recurrences develop at the edge of the surgical margin and a common reason for an early recurrence of a glioblastoma is when tumors are not completely resected. schema.label: Design
schema.text: Non-randomized phase II trial (SABR-5, NCT02933242). All participants receive stereotactic ablative radiotherapy to every site of progressing metastatic disease. The accrual target is 200 patients. The primary concern stated in the protocol is toxicity.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: SABR is delivered to all sites of active metastatic disease, with a maximum of five metastases. For non-brainstem metastases, single-fraction radiosurgery is limited to a maximum size of 3 cm. Lesions from 3.1 to 4 cm may be treated with 25 to 35 Gy in 5 fractions. Brain cases require stereotactic rounds approval. Other site-specific doses are printed in a protocol table whose grid did not extract as a reliable dose list, so those rows are not restated. The PTV volume receiving 100% of the prescription should equal 95%, and coverage may be reduced to meet organ-at-risk constraints. Patients are excluded if 100% coverage falls below 50% of the PTV.

brief.schema_source: Open-access protocol, Olson et al., BMC Cancer 2018 (PMID 30286739). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Age 18 or older, histologically confirmed malignancy, and at most five metastases eligible for SABR. The primary tumor has been treated radically or controlled by prior palliative radiotherapy or systemic therapy. Biopsy of a metastasis is preferred but not required.

Excluded: comorbidity precluding radiotherapy; femoral metastasis at high risk of fracture; one to three brain metastases and no disease elsewhere; complete response to first-line chemotherapy; persistent malignant pleural effusion; inability to treat every site of progressing disease; spinal cord compression; a dominant brain metastasis requiring surgical decompression; pregnancy or lactation.

during.window: From 48 hours before the first fraction until 48 hours after the last fraction
during.note: Cytotoxic, immunotherapy, or molecularly targeted agents are held. Some agents require a longer break. Hormonal therapy during SABR is allowed.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Nedaplatin 10 mg/body/day and 5-FU 500 mg/body/day as a continuous infusion for 20 days, given with fractionated radiotherapy. Radiotherapy starts on the first day of chemotherapy, five days a week, at 1.8 to 2.0 Gy per fraction, to a total dose of 50.4 to 66 Gy. After 40 Gy the field is changed to avoid the spinal cord, except in two patients. Additional nedaplatin and 5-FU after chemoradiotherapy is optional, for a maximum of five courses.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Multicenter randomized phase II trial testing whether stereotactic ablative radiotherapy to all liver metastases improves progression-free survival when added to first-line anti-PD-(L)1 therapy, with or without platinum chemotherapy, in metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer. The sample size is 68 patients.

schema.label: Entry
schema.text: Adults with newly diagnosed stage IV non-small-cell lung cancer involving the liver, without known EGFR, ALK, BRAF, or ROS1 alterations, ECOG 0-2, and liver metastases suitable for ablative radiotherapy. Patients may be enrolled up to the start of cycle 3 of immunotherapy.

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Patients are randomized 1:1. Liver radiotherapy should preferably finish before immunotherapy and must finish before cycle 3 or within 90 days of starting immunotherapy.

arms.label: Arm 1, systemic therapy
arms.text: Standard first-line anti-PD-(L)1 immunotherapy with or without platinum chemotherapy.

arms.label: Arm 2, systemic therapy plus liver SABR
arms.text: The same systemic therapy plus stereotactic ablative radiotherapy to every liver metastasis, 30 to 60 Gy in 3 to 6 fractions according to institutional standards and normal-liver dose.

brief.schema_source: Open-access HAMMER-NSCLC protocol (BMC Cancer, 2025) states the 1:1 randomization and the liver radiotherapy dose range.
eligibility: Age greater than 18, histologically confirmed stage IV non-small cell lung cancer without known EGFR or BRAF mutations or ALK or ROS1 rearrangements. KRAS alterations are allowed.
